Chemical Name of Ash: Magnesium Oxide
Reaction Type: Combination Reaction

questions.text_english: Where are auxins synthesized? How do they promote phototropism?

key_points: Synthesized in shoot tips.
Auxins diffuse towards the shaded side.
Cause cell elongation on the shaded side, bending the plant towards light.

questions.solution: Auxins are synthesized at the tips of shoots in plants. When light hits one side of the plant, auxins diffuse towards the shaded, opposite side. This uneven distribution causes the cells on the darker side to elongate more quickly, bending the shoot stem towards the direction of the light source, thus promoting phototropism.

key_points: Microorganisms that break down dead and decaying organic matter.

Consequence 2: Disruption of nutrient recycling.

questions.solution: Decomposers are microorganisms, such as bacteria and fungi, that break down complex dead organic matter into simpler inorganic substances. Furthermore, the vital recycling of nutrients back into the soil would cease, halting new plant growth.

questions.text_english: We water the soil but it reaches the topmost leaves of the plants. Explain in brief the process involved.

key_points: Roots absorb water from soil through osmosis.
Transpiration creates a suction pull.
Water moves upwards through xylem vessels.

questions.solution: When soil is watered, the root hair cells actively take up ions, creating a concentration gradient that draws water in via osmosis. From the roots, water enters the xylem tissue. The continuous evaporation of water from the leaves, known as transpiration, creates a powerful suction force called transpiration pull. This pull acts like a straw, dragging the continuous water column upward through the xylem vessels to reach the topmost leaves.

key_points: Brain and Spinal Cord.
Brain is protected by skull (cranium) and cerebrospinal fluid.
Spinal cord is protected by the vertebral column.

sub_questions.solution: The two main constituents of the Central Nervous System are the brain and the spinal cord. The brain is securely protected by a bony box called the cranium (skull) and a shock-absorbing cerebrospinal fluid. The spinal cord is protected by the bony vertebral column.

sub_questions.solution: First, electrical impulses only reach cells that are directly connected by nervous tissue, meaning they do not affect every cell in the body. key_points: Tyndall effect (scattering of light).
Fine particles scatter blue light.
Larger particles scatter light of longer wavelengths (red).
Very large particles scatter all colours making it appear white.

questions.solution: This phenomenon is known as the Tyndall effect. It occurs because the tiny smoke particles suspended in the room scatter the incoming beam of light in all directions, illuminating the path and making it visible. The colour of the scattered light depends heavily on the particle size. Very fine particles scatter shorter wavelengths, primarily blue light. Moderately larger particles tend to scatter longer wavelengths like red. If the particles are large enough, the scattered light appears white.

questions.text_english: Explain in brief the function of an electric fuse in a domestic circuit. Justify your answer with necessary calculation.

key_points: Fuse melts to break the circuit preventing over-current.

Since 13.63 A > 5 A, the fuse will blow.

questions.solution: An electric fuse acts as a vital safety device. It contains a wire with a low melting point that melts and breaks the circuit when the current exceeds a safe limit, preventing fires and protecting appliances. For the heater, the current drawn is I = Power/Voltage. Here, I = 3000 W / 220 V, which equals approximately 13.63 A. Since 13.63 A is significantly higher than the circuit's safe limit of 5 A, turning on the heater will immediately melt the fuse and break the circuit.

(ii) A 4 cm tall object is placed perpendicular to the principal axis of convex lens of focal length 24 cm. The distance of object from the lens is 16 cm. Find the position and size of image formed. sub_questions.text: (a) किरण आरेख और उत्तल लेंस का संख्यात्मक हल।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Ray diagrams and Convex lens numerical.

key_points: Ray parallel to axis diverges.
Ray towards focus becomes parallel.

sub_questions.solution: For a concave lens, a ray incoming parallel to the principal axis refracts outward, appearing to diverge from the principal focus. A ray directed towards the principal focus refracts to become parallel to the principal axis. For the numerical: We have object height h = 4 cm, focal length f = +24 cm, and object distance u = -16 cm. Using the lens formula 1/f = 1/v - 1/u, we get 1/v = 1/24 - 1/16. The common denominator is 48. Thus, 1/v = 2/48 - 3/48 = -1/48, meaning v = -48 cm. The image forms 48 cm on the same side as the object. The magnification m = v/u = (-48)/(-16) = +3. Hence, the image size h' = m * h = 3 * 4 = +12 cm. It is a virtual, erect, and magnified image.

sub_questions.text: (b) किरण आरेख और अवतल दर्पण का संख्यात्मक हल।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Ray diagrams and Concave mirror numerical.

key_points: Ray parallel to axis diverges.
Ray towards focus reflects parallel.

sub_questions.solution: For a convex mirror, a ray incoming parallel to the principal axis reflects outwards, appearing to come from the virtual principal focus behind the mirror. A ray directed towards the principal focus reflects and travels parallel to the principal axis. For the numerical part: For a concave mirror, focal length f = -12 cm, object distance u = -18 cm, and object height h = 1.5 cm. Using the mirror formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u, we rearrange to 1/v = 1/f - 1/u. So, 1/v = -1/12 - (-1/18) = -3/36 + 2/36 = -1/36. This gives v = -36 cm. The image forms 36 cm in front of the mirror. Magnification m = -v/u = -(-36)/(-18) = -2. The size of the image h' = m * h = -2 * 1.5 = -3.0 cm. The image is real, inverted, and magnified.

sub_questions.text: (a) मुख गुहा में उपस्थित ग्रंथियों का नाम लिखिए तथा भोजन के उस घटक का उल्लेख कीजिए जिस पर इन ग्रंथियों के स्राव क्रिया करते हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Name the glands present in the buccal cavity and write the components of food on which the secretion of these glands act upon.

key_points: Salivary glands.
They act upon complex carbohydrates (starch) converting them to sugar.

sub_questions.solution: The glands present in the buccal cavity are the salivary glands. They secrete saliva, which contains the enzyme salivary amylase. This enzyme acts upon complex carbohydrates, specifically starch, breaking it down into simpler sugars.

sub_questions.text: (b) दो अंगों में निकास पर अवरोधिनी पेशी होती हैं। इनका नाम लिखिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Two organs have a sphincter muscle at their exit. Name them.

key_points: Stomach.
Anus.

sub_questions.solution: Two key organs in the digestive tract that possess a sphincter muscle at their exit are the stomach (pyloric sphincter) and the anus (anal sphincter). These regulate the movement of food and waste.

sub_questions.text: (c) इनमें से किसी एक का उत्तर दें: (i) जठर ग्रंथियों द्वारा श्लेष्मा का स्रावण नहीं किया जाए ? (ii) क्षुद्रांत्र में दीर्घ रोम उपस्थित न हों ? अथवा पित्त रस का पाचन में महत्त्व।
sub_questions.text_english: Attempt either one of the given choices for part (c).

key_points: Option 1: Lack of mucus leads to stomach ulcers. Lack of villi decreases absorption.
Option 2: Bile emulsifies fats into smaller globules, making enzyme action efficient.

sub_questions.solution: Choice 1: If mucus is not secreted by the gastric glands, the highly acidic gastric juice would erode the inner lining of the stomach, potentially causing severe ulcers. If villi are absent in the small intestine, the surface area for absorption would drastically reduce, leading to poor nutrient absorption and malnutrition. Choice 2: Bile juice lacks digestive enzymes, yet it plays a crucial role by emulsifying large fat globules into smaller micelles, increasing the surface area for lipase action, and neutralizing stomach acidity to provide an alkaline medium for pancreatic enzymes.

sub_questions.text: (a) उल्लेख कीजिए क्या होता है जब (i) कुंजी K1 को बन्द करते हैं। (ii) कुंजी K2 को बन्द करते हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) State what happens when (i) key K1 is closed. (ii) key K2 is closed.

key_points: (i) Bulb A glows.
(ii) Bulbs B, C, D, E glow.

sub_questions.solution: When key K1 is closed, the circuit for bulb A is completed, so bulb A begins to glow. When key K2 is closed, the branch containing the four series bulbs (B, C, D, and E) is completed, causing all four of them to glow.

sub_questions.text: (b) जब बल्ब B चमक रहा होता है तब वह कितनी धारा लेता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Find the current drawn by the bulb B when it glows.
sub_questions.solution: The power rating of bulb B is 11 W and its voltage is 55 V. Since power P = V * I, the current I drawn by bulb B is 11 / 55, which equals 0.2 A.

sub_questions.text: (c) प्रतिरोध की गणना अथवा फ्यूज होने पर प्रभाव।
sub_questions.text_english: Attempt either one of the given choices for part (c).

key_points: Option 1: R_B = V^2/P = 275 ohms. Total series R = 4 * 275 = 1100 ohms.
Option 2: If C fuses, B, D, E stop glowing because the series circuit breaks. Bulb A continues to glow as it is in parallel.

sub_questions.solution: Choice 1: To calculate the resistance of bulb B, we use the formula R = V^2 / P. Thus, R_B = (55)^2 / 11 = 3025 / 11 = 275 ohms. Since bulbs B, C, D, and E are in series and identical, their total equivalent resistance is 4 * 275 = 1100 ohms. Choice 2: If bulb C suddenly gets fused while both keys are closed, the series branch circuit breaks. As a result, bulbs B, D, and E will stop glowing because no current can flow through that branch. However, bulb A remains unaffected and continues to glow brightly because it is connected in a separate parallel branch.
